Package org.jdesktop.lg3d.utils.taskscheduler

  • Related Packages

    Description
    org.jdesktop.lg3d.utils
     
  • Class
    Description
    CronExpression
    A parser and evaluator for crontab-style schedules, the timing core of the desktop TaskScheduler.
    MisfirePolicy
    What the TaskSchedulerEngine does when it discovers that a task's scheduled fire time passed while the desktop (and therefore the scheduler) was not running - the classic "misfire" a laptop that sleeps overnight hits.
    PrefsTaskStore
    The TaskStore backed by the user Preferences tree, following the same pattern as the desktop's other per-user stores.
    ProcessTaskRunner
    The production TaskRunner: it executes a ScheduledTask and captures the outcome as a TaskExecutionRecord.
    ScheduledTask
    One user-defined scheduled job: what to run, when to run it (a Trigger), and how the scheduler should behave around it (timeout, concurrency guard, misfire policy, retries).
    ScheduledTask.Action
    What a task actually does when it fires.
    TaskExecutionRecord
    An immutable record of one execution of a ScheduledTask, kept as the task's run history so the scheduler is auditable: what ran, when, how long it took, whether it succeeded, and a short, secret-free tail of its output.
    TaskExecutionRecord.Status
    How a single execution ended.
    TaskRunner
    Executes a ScheduledTask once and reports the outcome.
    TaskScheduler
    The desktop-wide entry point to the cron-style task scheduler: a process singleton that wires a PrefsTaskStore, a ProcessTaskRunner and a TaskSchedulerEngine together and exposes the small, safe API the Control-Centre panel and the desktop start-up use.
    TaskSchedulerEngine
    The reliable scheduling loop at the heart of the desktop task scheduler.
    TaskSchedulerEngine.Listener
    Notified when the task set changes or a task finishes a run.
    TaskStore
    Persistence for the desktop's scheduled tasks and their run history.
    TaskValidator
    Validates a ScheduledTask before it is persisted or run, so a bad or hostile definition is rejected at the boundary (the scheduler UI) rather than discovered - or worse, executed - later.
    Trigger
    When a ScheduledTask fires.
    Trigger.Kind
    The kind of schedule a Trigger represents.
